title: Model specifications
text: @annotated tag must used record compartments. Write OBS brackets define observation compartment(s). Also used obs_rows() fill ‘cmt’ column dataset. Write ADM brackets define “default” administration compartment(s). information used optimization process mapbayest() function. information mandatory use adm_rows() build dataset order automatically set value ‘cmt’ column. Especially useful use model absorption several depot compartment requiring duplicate administrations lines data set.
code: //example: model with dual zero and first order absorption in compartment 1 & 2, respectively, and observation of parent drug + metabolite  $CMT @annotated DEPOT: Depot [ADM] CENT_PAR: examplinib central [ADM, OBS] PERIPH : examplinib peripheral CENT_MET : methylexamplinib central [OBS]

title: Model specifications
text: Define least one $OMEGA block. Multiple blocks options (e.g. correlation, block etc) allowed.
code: $OMEGA 0.123 0.456 0.789 $OMEGA @annotated ECL : 0.123 : Clearance ETA2 : 0.456 : Volume of distribution FOO : 0.789 : Absorption rate constant // reminder: Each ETA can be described with (`@annotated`) // The labels (on the left-hand side) are not considered by mapbayr

title: Model specifications
text: definition $SIGMA block may straightforward blocks, tried keep simple possible. Keep mind mapbayr always expect pair sigma values type dependent variable: first value proportional error, second additive. Two situations can distinguished: one type concentration fit, use [OBS] assignment $CMT. Simply write one pair sigma values describe proportional additive error concentrations. error model automatically applied compartment observations recorded dataset (.e. value CMT MDV = 0). multiple types DV (parent metabolite), /used [OBS] assignment $CMT. Write many pairs sigma values compartments assigned [OBS] $CMT. order pair must respect order compartments assigned. put clearly, sigma matrix interpreted whatever model :
code: $SIGMA 0.111 0 // proportional error $SIGMA 0 0.222 // (log) additive error $SIGMA 0.333 0.444 // mixed error //example: correlated proportional error between parent and metabolite $SIGMA @block 0.050 // proportional error on parent drug 0.000 0.000 // additive error on parent drug 0.100 0.000 0.200 // proportional error on metabolite 0.000 0.000 0.000 0.000 // additive error on metabolite // reminder: sigma values can be recorded in multiple $SIGMA blocks

title: Model specifications
text: Refer concentration variable fit DV. Mind code, especially concentrations observed multiple compartments. Express log-additive error models exponential. way, concentrations automatically log-transformed optimization process, necessity prior log-transform concentration. fitting parent drug metabolite simultaneously, refer PAR MET, define DV accordingly (DV used optimization process, PAR MET variables mandatory post-processing internal functions) Note mapbayr strictly rely $ERROR block define residual error internally compute objective function value, information passed $SIGMA block. However, strongly advise properly code $ERROR block EPS(1), EPS(2) etc…, use code regular mrgsolve model code simulate random effects.

title: MAP-Bayesian Estimation of PK Parameters
code: code <- " $PARAM @annotated TVCL:  0.9 : Clearance TVV1: 10.0 : Central volume V2  : 10.0 : Peripheral volume of distribution Q   :  1.0 : Intercompartmental clearance  $PARAM @annotated @covariates BW : 70 : Body weight (kg)  $OMEGA 0.3 0.3 $SIGMA 0.05 // proportional 0.1 // additive  $CMT @annotated CENT  : Central compartment (mg/L)[ADM, OBS] PERIPH: Peripheral compartment ()  $TABLE double DV = (CENT/V1) *(1 + EPS(1)) + EPS(2);  $MAIN double CL = TVCL * exp(ETA(1)) * pow(BW / 70, 1.2) ; double V1 = TVV1 * exp(ETA(2)) ; double K12 = Q / V1  ; double K21 = Q / V2  ; double K10 = CL / V1 ;  $ODE dxdt_CENT   =  K21 * PERIPH - (K10 + K12) * CENT ; dxdt_PERIPH =  K12 * CENT - K21 * PERIPH ;  $CAPTURE DV CL "  my_model <- mcode("Example_model", code)

code: print(my_est) #> Model: Example_model  #> ID : 1 individual(s). #> OBS: 2 observation(s). #> ETA: 2 parameter(s) to estimate. #>  #> Estimates:  #>   ID      ETA1      ETA2 #> 1  1 0.3872104 0.1569604 #>  #> Output (4 lines):  #>   ID time evid cmt amt rate mdv  DV IPRED  PRED   CL BW  ETA1  ETA2 #> 1  1    0    1   1 100   20   1  NA 0.000 0.000 1.79 90 0.387 0.157 #> 2  1    6    0   1   0    0   0 3.9 4.162 5.174 1.79 90 0.387 0.157 #> 3  1   15    0   1   0    0   0 1.1 1.087 1.647 1.79 90 0.387 0.157 #> 4  1   24    0   1   0    0   1 2.0 0.556 0.959 1.79 90 0.387 0.157 plot(my_est) hist(my_est) # Easily extract a posteriori parameter values to compute outcomes of interest get_eta(my_est) #>      ETA1      ETA2  #> 0.3872104 0.1569604 get_param(my_est, "CL") #> [1] 1.79217  # The function `use_estimates()` updates the model object with estimated parameter values (ETA) and covariates to simulate like with a regular mrgsolve model  updated_model <- my_est %>%    use_estimates()   # Define simulation scenarios (let your inspiration flow) and simulate scenarios <- tibble::tibble(   ID = 1, time = 0, evid = 1, cmt = 1,   amt = c(50, 100, 200, 500),    rate = amt/5,    scenario = forcats::as_factor(paste0(amt, " mg")) )  simdat <- data.frame() for(i in unique(scenarios$scenario)){   simdat <- updated_model %>%      data_set(subset(scenarios, scenario == i)) %>%      mrgsim(output = "df", recover = "scenario") %>%      bind_rows(simdat) }  # See the results library(ggplot2) simdat %>%    ggplot(aes(time, DV)) +   geom_line(aes(color = scenario)) +   geom_point(data = my_data %>% dplyr::filter(mdv == 0)) +    theme_bw() +   scale_colour_discrete(palette = scales::pal_brewer(palette = "Dark2"))
